headline: On last trading day, Indian benchmarks posted longest weekly losing run in 25 years amid heavy FII selling.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: Persistent selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in the Indian equity market
Anticipation of a 25 bps repo rate hike by the RBI due to mounting inflation pressures
Concerns over the longest weekly losing streak in 25 years affecting investor sentiment
Expectations of slow conversion of deal wins in the IT sector ahead of Q2 results
whatHappening: Equity markets fell for eight consecutive weeks for the first time in 25 years
Sensex crashed 1,000 points in a single session, wiping out approximately ₹9 lakh crore in investor wealth
DMart reported Q2 revenue from operations exceeding ₹16,000 crore with an expanded network of 518 stores
DLF successfully completed a ₹1,985 crore sell-out of its senior living project
summary: Indian markets recorded an eight-week losing streak, the longest in 25 years, driven by heavy FII selling and inflation concerns. Investors remain cautious ahead of the RBI's October policy meeting and the upcoming Q2 earnings season. Despite the broader downturn, companies like DLF and DMart reported strong operational updates regarding project sales and revenue growth.
